A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Singular Bayesian Neural Networks, including Appendices A–I. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that 68 of 70 pages are identical; differences are confined to the version stamp and Appendix E.10.1. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on MIMIC-III, Beijing air quality and SST-2, plus appendix studies covering ensembling, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and synthetic regression.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark tables and the additional experiments in Appendices H and I.

M1.justification: The low-rank factorization, variational objective, posterior families, initialization, optimization and inference procedures are unchanged. The Appendix E.10.1 addition specifies no algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets and tasks, including newborn, Guangzhou and AG News OOD evaluations, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and synthetic regression. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including deterministic models, Deep Ensembles, Full-Rank BBB, Rank-1 multiplicative models and the supplementary SWAG comparisons.

E3.justification: The experimental descriptions retain identical splits, preprocessing, architectures, ranks, training budgets, metrics and Monte Carlo evaluation procedures across the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: The rank sweeps, singular-value analyses, selective prediction studies, uncertainty-distribution analyses, calibration-binning checks and low-rank ensembling study are unchanged.

E5.justification: Run counts, seeds, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and the single-run qualification for the ensembling study are unchanged. The new probability statement in Appendix E.10.1 concerns theory, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All empirical result entries and findings are identical. For example, Table 1 retains low-rank OOD AUROC of 0.802 ± 0.018, and Table 3 retains low-rank SST-2 accuracy of 0.806 ± 0.003.

T1.justification: Appendix E.10.1 adds a sufficient-condition statement absent from v3: sampled networks should remain uniformly close to a network formed from mean layer matrices on bounded inputs, with probability at least one half, when summed relative spectral-norm perturbations are sufficiently small. No quantitative threshold, supporting derivation or revision to an existing numbered theorem accompanies this addition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about singular posterior geometry, parameter efficiency, generalization bounds and task-dependent predictive and uncertainty performance.

C2.justification: The new Appendix E.10.1 passage explicitly explains that the perturbation condition constrains the sum across all layers, with no separate per-layer allowance. Existing empirical interpretations and limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Initialization details, hyperparameters, hardware, software, preprocessing instructions, training times and resource-access information are unchanged. The added theoretical passage supplies no implementation instructions.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list and research positioning, including Appendix A, are identical. The new passage introduces no cited work or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v4 expands one paragraph at the end of Appendix E.10.1 and updates the first-page version/date stamp. The remaining wording, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 41 adjusts vertical spacing and text/equation placement to accommodate the added passage. All figures, tables, captions, axes and legends remain identical.

improvement.justification: Relative to v3, the new Appendix E.10.1 passage clarifies the reference network and aggregation of perturbations across layers. However, it leaves 'sufficiently small' unquantified and does not derive the stated probability of at least one half. This limited clarity benefit comes with an underspecified theoretical assertion, so its net effect on quality is unclear. Existing proofs, experimental evidence and other substantive content are unchanged.
